sentences.text:
This application coming on for admission this day, the  following:
 ORDER Case Diary is perused.
The applicant has filed this First application u/S 438, Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail.
Applicant apprehends his arrest in connection with Crime No.54/2024 registered at Police Station Daboh, District Bhind for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 409 of IPC.

According to prosecution case, Sub-Divisional Officer Lahar, District Bhind received a complaint according to which allegations were levelled against 2 MCRC-17088-2024 the present applicant and other employees of Municipal Council Daboh to have embezzled money by transferring it to the accounts of ineligible persons under Sambal Yojana and Kanya Vivah Sahayat Scheme.

The Sub-Divisional Officer Lahar investigated the matter and statements of the Branch Raghvendra Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130538695/

sentences.text: 1 In-charge/applicant, operator posted there, Rizwan Khan and Ward-in-charge Pawan Savita were recorded.
All those persons narrated different versions about the bank statements.
It was found that an amount of Rs. 51000/- was deposited twice in the back account of one beneficiary Vikas Shivhare by manipulation.
The same manipulation was seen in many other cases.
On the basis of said investigation by SDO, a case was registered and investigation is being conducted.
It is the submission of learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is apprehending his arrest on the basis of registration of offence as above.
Confinement may bring social disrepute and personal inconvenience.
Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that applicant is innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in the matter.
Applicant is ready to cooperate in the investigation/trial and he is ready to abide by the terms and conditions as imposed over him.
Under these grounds, counsel prayed for grant of anticipatory bail.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent-State has opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection.
Heard counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court deems it fit to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.

Accordingly, the instant application is allowed and it is directed that without any prejudice to his defence, if the applicant deposits an amount of 3 MCRC-17088-2024 Rs.4,00,000/- (Rupees Four Lakh Only) through cheque within a period of 10 days then, in the event of his arrest, the applicant be released on bail on furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakh)
with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer).
The applicant will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be.
